web_evidence.title: Beautiful World, Where Are You?
web_evidence.note: The Sewanee Review explicitly describes alternating third-person chapters and first-person emails exchanged by Alice and Eileen.

web_evidence.title: Unread Messages
web_evidence.note: Rooney's authorized sustained fiction publication follows Eileen through extensive external she/her narration, corroborating the novel's third-person strand.

search_log: Searched "Beautiful World Where Are You Sally Rooney excerpt publisher chapters emails third person" and structural POV variants; located the Sewanee Review and official FSG reading guide.
Searched for authorized extracts on The New Yorker, Guardian, Penguin, and Faber; opened The New Yorker's sustained "Unread Messages" text.
Searched "Beautiful World Where Are You narrative structure alternating emails third person review" and related point-of-view queries; multiple reviews corroborated the alternating form.
Ran targeted exact-quotation searches for ambiguous clippings; most Goodreads quote pages lacked usable context, while the authorized New Yorker text established that q06418 is Aidan's speech.
person_note: The novel has two sustained base forms: nonparticipating third-person scene chapters and constitutive first-person emails written by Alice and Eileen. The official publisher guide and the Sewanee Review independently state this whole-book structure, while Rooney's authorized New Yorker text supplies sustained third-person prose. The quote set independently contains both story-specific first-person email narration and externally narrated third-person scenes. Dialogue and gnomic passages were not allowed to vote by pronoun; notably, q06418 is Aidan's speech despite its upstream event bucket. The only material residual uncertainty concerns attribution of a few isolated clippings such as q06402, not the documented alternating structure.
